summary: How echoes become a picture: timing, sweep, range rings, bearings, memory, ARPA and the display power supply.

blocks.title: Timing and sweep
items: Synchronizer (timer): develops synchronizing pulses for the transmitter system. Output: a pulse or square wave.
It primarily affects the modulator and initiates the sweep drive, together. Resolver output isn't affected.
Sweep generator: makes a sawtooth, the drive signal to the sweep amplifier.
Sweep amplifier: drives the 2 CRT deflection coils.
Video amplifier: provides composite video to the CRT cathode. Inputs: low-level video, fixed rings, variable ring. Not the resolver.

blocks.title: The screen
items: CRT, cathode ray tube: anode at 10 to 50 kV, about 17 kV in many radar displays.
Aquadag: graphite coating. Second anode, protects electrons from strong electric fields, attracts secondary emissions: all of the above.
Raster scan: the beam goes horizontally and vertically across the CRT face, controlled by clock pulses, with an address bus.
LCD, liquid crystal display: current passes through the crystals, aligning them. Greater than 200 pixels per inch.

items.name: Ring spacing
items.means: T = 1 ÷ f, and each cycle is 1 ring. Echoes take 12.34 µs per nautical mile.
items.example: 27 kHz: T = 37.04 µs, about 3 nautical miles

blocks.title: Range and bearing
items: Range markers are determined by the timer. A blocking oscillator gives their very narrow pulses.
VRM, variable range marker: a single adjustable ring, for accurate range of a moving target. Control: variable resistor. Key part: shift register. Signal feeds the video amplifier.
VRM accuracy: align minimum and maximum ranges with matching fixed rings.
EBL, electronic bearing line: a line from own vessel to a specific target, measuring its bearing.
Gyro signals give own heading and are required to indicate azimuth.
True bearing: north at the top; heading flasher indicates the vessel's course.
Bearing resolution: telling apart 2 adjacent targets of equal distance.

blocks.title: Memory and processing
items: Digitized sweep: 360° divided into 4,096 segments.
Display memory: mainly eliminates fluctuating targets such as sea return.
Dual memory: successive sweeps are digitized and compared; only signals in both display, so 2 sequential cells.
Digital processing: major advantage is enhancement of weak target returns.
Analog-to-digital sampling: greater than 2 times the highest component.

items.def: dynamic random access memory. Charges leak, so it needs a REFRESH cycle.

blocks.title: Exam traps
items: Collision computer inputs: position, heading, speed. Not wind from an anemometer.
Own speed stuck on manual: LOG OUT.
RC integrator, square wave, period far under 1 time constant: triangle wave.
Removing stationary objects: discriminator as second detector.
The exam rounds 3.085 µs to 3.1 µs, giving 322 kHz.
Pulse forming network voltage isn't a display supply output.
